A screen has a big impact on how a device feels to use. It determines how crisp text looks on your laptop, how smoothly fast-moving games appear on your monitor, how long your phone lasts on a charge, and whether the person next to you on the train can read your screen. OLED screens, in particular, need a lot of precision to manufacture, which is why they’re most often found only in higher-end phones, laptops, monitors, and tablets.

TCL CSOT, which makes and develops displays for many device manufacturers, is working on a method to build OLED panels by printing the materials onto them, which could help OLED get into more products.

At DTC 2026, its annual Global Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference in Wuhan, China, on November 13, TCL CSOT showcased its latest display tech: inkjet-printed OLED, a 500Hz gaming monitor, a 115-inch 16K screen that shows 3D without glasses, and more. They also took Android Authority on a tour of the Wuhan factory and the t12 production line, where they’re working on the IJP OLED. Here’s what you need to know.

How inkjet-printed OLED works

TCL CSOT

IJP OLED stands for inkjet-printed OLED. While traditional OLED manufacturing uses processes to deposit organic materials onto the display, IJP OLED uses specialized printers to place those materials precisely where they’re needed. The idea is similar to using a home inkjet printer, but the “ink” is made of organic materials that form a working OLED panel.

Printing the materials this way helps reduce waste and potentially lower manufacturing costs, which is a significant advantage for bringing OLED to a wider range of products in the future.

It also offers a picture-quality benefit. IJP OLED uses TCL CSOT’s Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement, with separate red, green, and blue subpixels arranged in stripes. This design delivers sharper text and noticeably reduces color fringing around the edges of text and graphics compared with a conventional OLED panel.

TCL CSOT

Interview with Weiran Cao, Ph.D, at DTC 2026

With IJP OLED, we can reach 163 PPI on a 27-inch 4K display. For gaming displays, it can reach 218 PPI, with a 0.03 millisecond response time. People read a lot of text on monitors and laptops, so this is a benefit users can see every day.Weiran Cao, Ph.D, General Manager of IJP-OLED Middle Platform of TCL CSOT

TCL CSOT has already begun mass-producing IJP OLED panels, and several partner devices using this tech were featured at DTC 2026. The Lenovo Legion R9000P has a 16-inch IJP OLED panel with a 2,560×1,600 resolution, a 240Hz refresh rate, and 100% DCI-P3 coverage. Meanwhile, Lenovo’s ThinkVision P27UL-40 is the company’s first IJP OLED monitor for commercial use, with a 27-inch 4K display and 99% DCI-P3 coverage. The MSI Prestige 14 AI+ and MSI PRO MAX OLED 271UPJW12 also use TCL CSOT’s printed panels.

TCL CSOT has also introduced two new 14-inch IJP OLED notebook panels. One is less than 0.66mm thick, weighs under 66g, and has a reflectance of less than 1%. The other eliminates the cover glass, using a hardened polarizer with an 8H rating instead, but it still feels like glass to the touch, whether you use a finger or a stylus.

A 500Hz gaming monitor and a 115-inch 3D TV display

TCL CSOT

TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch QHD gaming monitor featuring an IJP OLED panel with an oxide backplane, and supporting refresh rates of up to 500Hz. TCL CSOT says it’s the first display to use in-panel compensation for high refresh rates. It helps maintain picture quality and runs in real time in the background, so there’s no need for the periodic power-off cycles used by conventional methods.

Real Stripe RGB keeps edges sharp, with a response time under 1ms. The 500Hz refresh rate is designed for competitive gaming, keeping moving targets in fast-paced shooters crisp and easy to track.

TCL CSOT

The 115-inch display has a native 16K resolution of 15,360×7,680, and TCL CSOT says it is the world’s highest image quality 16K 2D/3D-compatible light-field TV display. Its light-field optical architecture addresses the viewing-angle limitations of conventional glasses-free 3D, offering a 90-degree viewing angle or more, extended depth of field, and support for multiple viewers, so you don’t have to sit in one specific spot. The 3D light-field resolution reaches up to 8K, and the screen can switch between 2D and 3D, with TCL CSOT claiming there’s no loss in 2D picture quality.

The recommended viewing distance is 2–4m (6.5–13ft), making it well suited for private theatres, digital museums, interactive gaming, and premium showrooms. It’s an impressive display, though it’s unlikely to find its way into living rooms anytime soon.

More efficient and more private mobile displays

TCL CSOT

The 6.36-inch blue phosphorescent OLED may have been one of the most practical displays at DTC 2026. TCL CSOT says it’s the first smartphone OLED display to use a blue phosphorescent material system, which they say delivers roughly 40% higher luminous efficiency and around 20% lower electroluminescent power consumption at the same brightness.

The display is a major power draw, so the battery-life improvements are definitely exciting. Paired with the larger batteries introduced in newer handsets, more efficient screens could significantly increase the time you can use your device between charges. TCL CSOT is also working to refine materials and manufacturing processes to extend device lifetimes and bring blue phosphorescent displays to more devices.

TCL CSOT

The World’s First Full-Angle Lossless Privacy OLED Tablet Display(10.95″) helps keep your screen private from people nearby. Its dual-pixel architecture and pixel-level light-path control provide 360-degree active privacy while keeping the view clear from the front.

APEX and AI for Real

TCL CSOT

All of these technologies are part of APEX, TCL CSOT’s advanced display technology brand, created with picture quality, eye comfort, and sustainability in mind. APEX is built on four pillars: Amazing Display Experience, Protective of Eye Health, Eco-friendly to Build and Use, and Unlimited Imaginative Potential.

AI for Real was another major focus at DTC 2026. TCL’s strategy is to bring AI out of the lab and into everyday life. For TCL CSOT, a key part of that vision is Display for AI — advancing display technology so AI-powered devices can deliver a better experience. Whatever an AI assistant does on your phone or laptop, the screen is where you see the results and respond. That means better displays can make AI features feel more useful in your day-to-day life.

Know more about TCL CSOT at DTC 2026

TCL CSOT

At DTC 2026, TCL CSOT showed off its progress on several fronts. IJP OLED is moving beyond the demo stage and toward mass production, while gaming panels are advancing toward 500Hz. The company also showcased a 115-inch glasses-free 3D screen, along with new mobile panels that use less power and help keep your screen private. Bringing these efforts together is AI, which is helping TCL CSOT design displays much faster. And the great news is that many of these features are already in everyday use.

TCL CSOT makes panels for other device makers, so you can find its technology in products from a range of brands. IJP OLED is already featured in Lenovo and MSI laptops and monitors showcased at DTC 2026. The other displays are currently technology demonstrations, with no retail timelines announced yet. You can find more information about TCL CSOT’s display technology on its website.

OnePlus 15 and 15R ColorOS 17 update adds auto PC unlocking, smarter photo storage, and more

ColorOS users are catching up with their OxygenOS counterparts.

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 2:06 AM ET

•

•

Tushar Mehta / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• OnePlus is rolling out a ColorOS 17 update to the OnePlus 15 and 15R that adds automatic PC unlocking through the O Plus Connect app.

• The update also lets users free up storage by removing backed-up photos, customize image quality and resolution, and connect their phone and tablet to the same PC at the same time.

• Both phones get Calculator, Translate, and privacy improvements, alongside the November 2026 security patch.

Earlier this month, OnePlus rolled out an OxygenOS 16 update that lets your phone automatically unlock your PC when connecting remotely. ColorOS users missed out on this feature at the time, receiving translation improvements instead. That’s changing with the latest ColorOS 17 update for the OnePlus 15 and 15R, which brings automatic PC unlocking, November 2026 security patches, and several other useful additions.

With the update, O Plus Connect can use a saved password to automatically unlock your computer during a remote connection, saving you the trouble of entering it manually. To set this up, tap the More icon on the floating ball during a remote connection, select Unlock PC, and enable “Automatically unlock when connected.” The update also lets you connect your phone and tablet to the same PC at the same time.

OnePlus is also making it easier to manage photo storage. While the company integrated Google Photos support into its native gallery app back in 2024, the latest update adds a handy storage management tool. Once your photos are backed up to the cloud, you can remove the local copies to free up space without losing the backups. You can also choose the resolution and image quality when saving edited photos, letting you create smaller files for sharing.

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

The Calculator app now displays previous calculations on its main screen, allowing you to easily resume them. It also has a revised button layout and better-organized unit conversion tools. The Translate app also picks up some new superpowers: it now provides more detailed word lookups, including pronunciation, grammar, and usage examples, and adapts sentence translations to the appropriate writing style.

There’s also a new privacy setting that automatically takes you to the home screen when you exit a hidden app. Fluid Cloud cards on the lock screen and in the notification drawer are getting a translucent gradient effect.

The OnePlus 15’s November update changelog lists an additional feature that the Google Phone app has supported since 2021: incoming call announcements. With this enabled, you can hear who’s calling without looking at your phone. The feature isn’t mentioned in the 15R changelog.

Both updates include the November 2026 Android security patch and are rolling out in batches.

items.summary: The app's development is far from over.

Mobile

Samsung Messages could soon find, send, and forward texts for you

The app's development is far from over.

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 12:45 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 is rolling out in South Korea with groundwork for hands-free message management.

• The update also hints at smarter message searches and the ability to check how received photos were created or edited.

• Similar capabilities were spotted in China in September, but global versions of Samsung Messages still lack these additions.

Samsung may have shut down its Messages app in the US in July, but that hasn’t stopped the company from developing new features for users elsewhere. The latest update rolling out in South Korea suggests Samsung is preparing its texting app for a future where AI assistants can do much more than help you write messages.

As Sam Updater spotted, Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 introduces support for 10 functions that AI assistants such as Gemini could use to interact directly with the app. These include drafting, sending, replying to, forwarding, searching for, and deleting messages, as well as looking up contacts.

Rather than opening Samsung Messages and scrolling through conversations to find a discount code a retailer sent you last week, for example, you could simply ask your AI assistant to find it. Similarly, you could ask it to find a particular message and forward it to someone without navigating the app yourself.

The additions are particularly interesting given our recent discovery of Samsung Galaxy Claw, an upcoming AI experience that could perform tasks on your behalf across several apps, including Messages.

The update also lays the groundwork for smarter message searches that understand the meaning of your queries rather than relying solely on matching keywords. Additionally, there’s evidence of support for Content Credentials, a feature that Google Messages already offers to help users determine how received media was created or edited, including whether AI was involved.

Joe Maring / Android Authority

However, downloading the latest Samsung Messages update doesn’t necessarily mean you can start using all these features today. The findings come from an analysis of the app’s code, and the features haven’t been demonstrated in action.

There’s also the question of availability. The update is reportedly being offered to select Galaxy phones running One UI 9.0 in South Korea, including Ultra models dating back to the Galaxy S23. China received similar groundwork in September, but even users running the newer One UI 9.5 beta in Europe and India are still on an older version of the app without these additions.

While there’s no indication that Samsung plans to reverse its decision to discontinue Messages in the US, it’s clear that the app’s development is far from over in markets where it remains available.

ANBERNIC’s next Snapdragon-powered Game Boy-like handheld comes with active cooling

A more affordable RG 477V? One can hope.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 11:24 PM ET

•

•

ANBERNIC / YouTube

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• ANBERNIC has started teasing another new Android gaming handheld: the RG 47G1.

• It will come with a Snapdragon G1 Gen 2 chipset, a 5,500mAh battery, and active cooling.

• It will also feature a 4.7-inch 4:3 display with a 120Hz refresh rate.

ANBERNIC already has several Android handhelds in its portfolio, and the company isn’t shying away from adding more. After announcing the yet-to-be-released RG DDS, ANBERNIC has now started teasing a new vertical handheld: the RG 47G1.

In a new YouTube video, ANBERNIC teased the upcoming RG 47G1 and shared a few key details about what we’ll find under the hood. For starters, the RG 47G1 will feature a 4.7-inch display with a 1,280 x 960 pixel resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate. It will also pack in the Snapdragon G1 Gen 2 chipset, which we’ve seen on the ANBERNIC RG 55G1, and a 5,500mAh battery with an active cooling system. The teaser also showcases the handheld in three colors: Pika Yellow, Retro Purple, and Black.

ANBERNIC hasn’t said anything about when the RG 47G1 could be released or how much it could cost. However, based on the specs we’ve seen so far, it seems like the RG 47G1 will be an RG 477V with a Snapdragon chipset replacing the Dimensity 8300. We’ve already seen the Snapdragon G1 Gen 2’s performance on the RG 55G1 and the Retroid Pocket Classic, and it’s an entry-level chip that performs quite well in emulation, so we’re expecting performance in line with those devices, and hopefully a similar price.

That said, it’s worth noting that rising memory prices could play a role in the RG 47G1’s pricing when it is released. Hopefully, it won’t go so high that it approaches the RG 477V’s price, which would put it in dangerous territory.

Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting

Android just recorded its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, with Apple's iOS bucking the trend.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 10:41 PM ET

•

•

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Android accounted for 74% of global smartphone sales in Q3 2026, down five points from a year ago and its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, per Counterpoint Research.

• iOS climbed to a record Q3 share of 21% as iPhone sales grew year-on-year, even as the overall market shrank 16%.

• HarmonyOS held at 5% globally and took 22% of China’s market, with HUAWEI growing 12% while China’s market shrank 10%.

The memory shortage has been dragging down phone sales all year, and new data shows it may be hurting Android more than its rivals.

According to Counterpoint Research, global smartphone sales fell 16% year-on-year in Q3 2026, a sharper drop than the 11% decline seen in Q2. Android’s share of those sales slipped to 74%, down from 79% in Q3 2025. That’s the lowest share Android has ever posted in a third quarter, though it’s still a touch above the 72% it hit in Q4 2025, when new iPhones typically give Apple a seasonal bump.

Counterpoint blames the RAM supply crisis, which has hit entry-level phones the hardest and pushed up prices in higher tiers. Because Android phones span every price segment, including the budget end where the squeeze has been worst, the platform has been more exposed to the slowdown than iOS. The firm says flagship launches from OPPO, vivo, and Xiaomi, along with Samsung’s latest foldables, helped soften the blow.

iPhones are bucking the trend

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

Apple, meanwhile, is having a good year in a bad market. iOS reached 21% of global sales in Q3 2026, its highest-ever share for a third quarter. iPhone sales actually grew 2% year-on-year while the overall market shrank 16%. Counterpoint credits the iPhone 18 Pro series, which it says outperformed the iPhone 17 Pro series, and notes that demand held up despite price increases across the iPhone lineup.

Meanwhile, HUAWEI’s HarmonyOS held steady at 5% of global sales. In China, it captured 22% of the market as the company’s sales grew 12% year-on-year, even as China’s overall market shrank 10%. The Enjoy 90 Pro Max, Nova 16, and Mate 80 series led the way, though Counterpoint warns that HUAWEI’s September price hikes could slow that momentum next quarter. HarmonyOS’s China share is down slightly from the record 24% it hit in Q2.

How Android fared in the US and other major markets

Here’s how the three markets Counterpoint tracks broke down in Q3 2026:

In the US, iOS pulled back ahead with 54% of sales, up from a near-even 51% in Q2, though Android’s 46% is still a point better than its 45% in Q3 2025. In China, Android recovered slightly to 60% from 58% in Q2, as HarmonyOS dipped. India remains firmly Android territory at 92%, unchanged from a year ago.

The bigger picture isn’t great for Android makers. Most major brands have reportedly cut their 2027 shipment targets, with vivo and Xiaomi trimming theirs by roughly a quarter, while Apple’s reported cut is far smaller. With memory prices not expected to ease until late 2027 at the earliest, budget Android phones, the segment that has historically powered Android’s dominance, look set to stay under pressure for a while yet.

OnePlus reveals ColorOS 17 plans for native apps, paid AI features, and more

More native apps are coming, but some AI features will cost you.

•

•

•

Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• OnePlus is exploring wider availability of its native Phone app and plans to bring OPPO’s Calendar app to its devices.

• ColorOS 17 users can pay for additional AI usage or wait for their free allowance to reset.

• OnePlus plans to add AI Photo Agent in a future update but has confirmed the removal of its iconic Calculator Easter egg.

The transition from OxygenOS to ColorOS has brought plenty of changes to OnePlus phones. And while many of our readers have warmed up to the new software, not everything has been well received by fans. From missing features to the future of native OnePlus apps, the company has now addressed some of the biggest questions surrounding ColorOS 17, revealing what users can expect from future updates and what’s already gone for good.

In a recent AMA on the OnePlus Community forum, OnePlus revealed that it’s exploring plans to bring its native dialer to more markets. Many OnePlus phones ship with Google Phone, while users in markets like India have access to the company’s own calling app, complete with features such as call recording without an audible announcement, AI-powered call summaries, and real-time translations. More users could eventually ditch Google’s dialer, although availability, including call recording support, will depend on the device and region.

Joe Maring / Android Authority

The company is also considering bringing OPPO’s Calendar app to OnePlus phones, giving users another alternative to Google’s stock apps. Neither app has a confirmed timeline for wider availability.

OnePlus also shed some light on the cost of using its AI features, something we touched on in our recent ColorOS 17 hands-on with the OnePlus 15. While some features will remain free, others will have free usage limits. Once you exhaust your allowance, you’ll have two options: pay for additional usage or wait for your allowance to reset. The company hasn’t specified how much additional usage will cost or how frequently these allowances will reset.

As for the AI features themselves, OnePlus plans to introduce AI Photo Agent in a future update. The feature lets you edit photos using natural language commands, much like Google Photos’ Help Me Edit. Meanwhile, AI Mind Pilot availability will vary by device, software version, and region. The company is also evaluating whether it can bring 3D and AI Motion Wallpapers to more phones.

OPPO

Music lovers wondering why lyrics aren’t showing up on their lock screens may have their streaming apps to blame. ColorOS 17 already supports the functionality, but music apps need to share lyrics with the system. OnePlus is working with app developers to expand compatibility.

Meanwhile, those experiencing increased battery drain or overheating after updating are advised to give their phones time to complete background optimizations. OnePlus hasn’t promised better battery life across all devices, but it says ColorOS 17 includes improvements to reduce micro-stutters during scrolling, app switching, and other everyday tasks.

Unfortunately, one familiar OnePlus feature isn’t making the transition to ColorOS. Typing “1+” followed by the equals button in the Calculator app will no longer bring up the iconic Never Settle Easter egg. It was among the little touches we highlighted when previewing what OnePlus users stood to lose with the switch to ColorOS, and OnePlus has now officially confirmed it’s gone.

Wearables and health

Samsung is bringing Galaxy Watch 9 health features to older Galaxy Watches

Even Galaxy Watch 4 owners aren't being left behind.

•

•

•

Adamya Sharma / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

TL;DR

• Samsung is bringing six Galaxy Watch 9 health and fitness features to the Galaxy Watch 8 series.

• The upgrades include Heart Health Score, Vitals, Daily Cardio Load, Fitness Index, improved Sleep Coaching, and enhanced sleep apnea detection.

• Select features also support older models, with improved Sleep Coaching extending back to the Galaxy Watch 4.

Samsung could break its tradition of launching a new Galaxy Watch every year as early as 2027, reportedly shifting its focus to software updates and new health features for existing smartwatches. We’re already seeing what that approach could mean for Galaxy Watch owners, as Samsung has confirmed that several health and fitness features from the Galaxy Watch 9 are making their way to last year’s models.

The company began rolling out stable One UI 9 Watch to the Galaxy Watch 8 series in mid-November, with US users receiving the update shortly after. In a new announcement, Samsung has detailed six health and fitness upgrades originally introduced with the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 that are coming to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic.

Vitals tracks five overnight health metrics, including heart rate, skin temperature, and blood oxygen, to flag unusual changes in your readings. Heart Health Score, meanwhile, helps you understand how everyday habits like sleeping and exercising affect your heart. For fitness enthusiasts, Daily Cardio Load helps balance training and recovery, while Fitness Index assesses your overall fitness and suggests exercises based on your goals.

Brady Snyder / Android Authority

Samsung is also improving Sleep Coaching, which now requires just three nights of data within two weeks to offer personalized guidance. The advice adapts weekly as your sleeping habits change.

Earlier this month, Samsung began rolling out enhanced sleep apnea detection to its latest wearables, promising support for older Galaxy Watches. That upgrade is now reaching the Watch 8 series, offering three categories of breathing disruption frequency. Other additions include the Portrait Watch Face and an improved Compass that lets you save important locations and retrace your steps.

Perhaps even better, Samsung confirms that Daily Cardio Load and Fitness Index support the Galaxy Watch 7 running One UI 9 Watch, while the improved Sleep Coaching experience goes back as far as the Galaxy Watch 4.

Some features require separate updates to Samsung Health or Samsung Health Monitor, and availability may vary by region.

Whether or not Samsung skips next year’s smartwatch launch, bringing these features to hardware that can already support them gives existing Galaxy Watch owners fewer reasons to spend money on a new model.

The company began rolling out stable One UI 9 Watch to the Galaxy Watch 8 series in mid-November, with US users receiving the update shortly after. In a new announcement, Samsung has detailed six health and fitness upgrades originally introduced with the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 that are coming to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic.

Vitals tracks five overnight health metrics, including heart rate, skin temperature, and blood oxygen, to flag unusual changes in your readings. Heart Health Score, meanwhile, helps you understand how everyday habits like sleeping and exercising affect your heart. For fitness enthusiasts, Daily Cardio Load helps balance training and recovery, while Fitness Index assesses your overall fitness and suggests exercises based on your goals.

blocks.alt: The Energy score on a Samsung Galaxy Watch 8.

blocks.text: Brady Snyder / Android Authority
Samsung is also improving Sleep Coaching, which now requires just three nights of data within two weeks to offer personalized guidance. The advice adapts weekly as your sleeping habits change.

Earlier this month, Samsung began rolling out enhanced sleep apnea detection to its latest wearables, promising support for older Galaxy Watches. That upgrade is now reaching the Watch 8 series, offering three categories of breathing disruption frequency. Other additions include the Portrait Watch Face and an improved Compass that lets you save important locations and retrace your steps.

Perhaps even better, Samsung confirms that Daily Cardio Load and Fitness Index support the Galaxy Watch 7 running One UI 9 Watch, while the improved Sleep Coaching experience goes back as far as the Galaxy Watch 4.
Some features require separate updates to Samsung Health or Samsung Health Monitor, and availability may vary by region.

Whether or not Samsung skips next year’s smartwatch launch, bringing these features to hardware that can already support them gives existing Galaxy Watch owners fewer reasons to spend money on a new model.

XGIMI Vibe One battery-powered projector hits a record low under $200

XGIMI's portable Vibe One projector is 24% off on Amazon, with Google TV, official Netflix, and a built-in battery.

•

XGIMI’s fun, battery-powered projector just dropped to its lowest price. The XGIMI Vibe One is down to $189 on Amazon, which is $60 off its $249 list price and a new record low.

The Vibe One is designed for grab-and-go entertainment. It has a built-in battery, so you can carry it to the bedroom, a friend’s place, or the backyard without hunting for an outlet, and its stand doubles as a handle. XGIMI rates the battery at up to 1.2 hours of video, which covers a short movie or a few episodes.

It projects a 1080p image and runs Google TV with official Netflix, so you can jump straight into streaming apps without a separate device. Auto focus and auto keystone correction keep setup quick, and the stand lets you tilt the projector to aim the picture where you want it.

The XGIMI Vibe One also works as a Bluetooth speaker when you’re not watching anything, and XGIMI includes stickers in the box so you can customize its look.

It’s rated at 250 lumens, so it’s best suited to darker rooms and evening viewing. The deal is from a third-party seller, but the order ships from Amazon.

At $189, it’s a playful, affordable projector that makes a great gift for teens, college students, or anyone who wants a simple movie night setup.
